title: Cosmos DB Data Modeling
description: Design effective data models for Cosmos DB using JSON documents, properties, and item patterns.

data.text: Cosmos DB data modeling is different from relational modeling. Instead of normalizing data across tables, you often **denormalize** related data into a single JSON document. This reduces the number of round trips needed for common queries and keeps your application simpler.

In the SQL API, each item is a JSON document with an `id` property. Every document also has a `_etag` for optimistic concurrency and system-defined metadata. You decide the schema, so each item in the same container can have different properties.

data.title: Patterns
items: **Embed for one-to-few** — embed small, bounded arrays directly in the document (e.g., order items inside an order).
**Reference for one-to-many** — store related items in a separate container and reference by id when the relationship is unbounded.
**Duplicate for read-heavy** — copy frequently accessed data across multiple containers if it avoids expensive joins.
**Use arrays and objects** — JSON lets you nest structures naturally, so avoid flat tables unless queries demand it.

terms.definition: A single JSON document in a Cosmos DB container, analogous to a row in a relational table.
Including related data directly in a document to reduce query complexity and improve read performance.
A system property used for optimistic concurrency control to prevent lost updates.

data.title: Model for Your Queries
data.text: Design your document structure around how you read data, not how you would write it relationally. Cosmos DB is optimized for single-item reads and queries within a partition.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cosmos DB uses schema-less JSON documents.
Denormalize related data to minimize round trips.
Choose embedding vs referencing based on cardinality and query patterns.
Every item needs an id and a partition key value.
data.takeaway: Good Cosmos DB modeling is about optimizing for fast, single-partition reads.
